Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=5{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+1,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=0,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(5{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+1)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Recall  ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1,$ so we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}5{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+1 & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2({sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2x))+1 \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{9}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{9}{2}x)\,|}_{-\pi /2}^{0} \\  & =(\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡0+\frac{9}{2}\cdot 0)-(\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi )+\frac{9}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =(0+0)-(0-\frac{9\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The area of the region is given by A=∫−π/20(5cos2⁡(2x)+2sin2⁡(2x)+1)dx.

Recall cos2⁡x+sin2⁡x=1, so we have 5cos2⁡(2x)+2sin2⁡(2x)+1=3cos2⁡(2x)+2(sin2⁡(2x)+cos2⁡(2x))+1=3cos2⁡(2x)+3.

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the cos2⁡x term, given by cos⁡2x=2cos2⁡x−1.

Rearranging, we have 2cos2⁡x=cos⁡2x+1.

Hence, the area of the region is A=∫−π/20(3cos2⁡(2x)+3)dx=∫−π/20(32(cos⁡4x+1)+3)dx=∫−π/20(32cos⁡4x+92)dx=(38sin⁡4x+92x)|−π/20=(38sin⁡0+92⋅0)−(38sin⁡(−2π)+92⋅(−π2))=(0+0)−(0−9π4)=9π4.
